subject: Computer Networking
title: Power over Ethernet (PoE)
description: A quick, practical guide to Power over Ethernet (PoE).

hook.text: What if one cable delivered both data and power? That's Power over Ethernet.

buildup.text: PoE sends DC power over the same copper pairs that carry Ethernet data. Devices extract what they need.

discovery.text: PoE powers IP cameras, Wi-Fi access points, VoIP phones, and IoT sensors. No separate outlet needed.

twist.text: PoE+ delivers 30 watts. PoE++ delivers 90 — enough for monitors, thin clients, and some laptops.

climax.text: A PoE switch powers a whole floor of APs from the server closet. One cable per device simplifies everything.

punchline.text: One cable, two jobs: data and power. PoE simplifies everything.

quiz.question: How much power can PoE++ deliver per port?

details.summary: Power over Ethernet delivers both data and electrical power over a single Ethernet cable, eliminating the need for separate power outlets at each device. PoE powers access points, IP cameras, VoIP phones, and IoT sensors with up to 90 watts per port on the latest PoE++ standard.
details.whyItMatters: PoE dramatically simplifies deployment of network devices by removing the need for electrical outlets at every installation point. It reduces cabling costs and enables device placement in locations without power access.
takeaways: PoE delivers data and power over a single Ethernet cable
PoE++ supports up to 90 watts for high-power devices
Centralized power management enables remote device restarting

faq.question: What devices commonly use Power over Ethernet?
faq.answer: Wireless access points, IP security cameras, VoIP phones, and IoT sensors are the most common PoE devices. PoE++ can power small displays, point-of-sale terminals, and even some thin client computers. Any low-power network device benefits from PoE deployment.

faq.question: What is the difference between PoE, PoE+, and PoE++?
faq.answer: PoE (802.3af) provides up to 15.4 watts per port. PoE+ (802.3at) doubles that to 30 watts. PoE++ (802.3bt) delivers up to 60 or 90 watts depending on the type. Higher wattage standards power more demanding devices like pan-tilt-zoom cameras and digital signage.
